plan.title: Adipose treated vs control DE with sex/age covariates
plan.analytical_narrative:
The input is a single-batch bulk RNA-seq experiment in human adipose tissue: raw Salmon gene-level counts for 12,000 gene symbols across 12 samples (counts.csv, 12000 x 13 with a gene-symbol first column) and a 12 x 4 sample table (metadata.csv) carrying condition (6 treated vs 6 control), sex (F/M) and age (years). The research question is simply which genes differ between treated and control, but the user flags two nuisance sources: sex differs between subjects and the groups are NOT age-matched. Age imbalance across the very variable of interest is the crux — it makes the naive ~condition contrast confounded, while adding age to the model costs a residual degree of freedom from an already tiny n=6 per group and, if the imbalance is severe, inflates the standard error of the condition coefficient through collinearity.

The plan therefore starts with an explicit design diagnostic (T1S1) rather than assuming: quantify the sex split per group, the age distribution per group and the condition~age association (point-biserial correlation, variance inflation for condition in ~condition+sex+age), plus library-size and PCA/clustering QC on VST values to see whether any covariate, not condition, drives the dominant variance axis. That diagnostic is a prerequisite, not decoration — it determines how much the covariate-adjusted result can be trusted and is required to interpret everything downstream.

T1S2 runs the primary analysis: DESeq2 on the raw integer counts with design ~sex + age + condition, treated vs control, independent filtering, Benjamini-Hochberg FDR and apeglm/ashr LFC shrinkage for ranking. Sex is a factor, age a continuous covariate centered for interpretability. The covariate-adjusted model is designated primary precisely because the groups are not age-matched. T1S3 is the robustness arm the design demands: the same contrast fit with (a) ~condition alone, (b) ~sex+condition, (c) ~sex+age+condition, and (d) limma-voom with the full covariate model, then compared gene-by-gene — concordance of the significant sets, rank correlation of test statistics, and how far individual log2 fold changes move when age enters. Genes whose call flips between the naive and adjusted models are exactly the ones most likely to be age-driven rather than treatment-driven, and they are reported as such.

T1S4 places the surviving signal in biological context with hallmark and GO gene sets for human, using both a ranked GSEA on the full shrunken-LFC ranking (which does not depend on an arbitrary FDR cut, important when n=6 per group may yield few genes past FDR 0.05) and over-representation on the DE set if one exists. With 12 samples the study is underpowered; every step is instructed to report effect sizes and confidence intervals alongside p-values, and to state plainly if the DE list is empty rather than relaxing thresholds to manufacture hits.
